thread:
Julia (Support): quick heads-up — customer reports sudden 250–400ms extra latency this morning. they say requests are landing in eu-west instead of us-west even though their SDK sets x-client-region=us-west :confused:
RouterBot: incoming routing log snippet (router-id=rt-42):
```
  ts=2026-03-15T09:20:11Z src=10.0.0.45 method=POST route=/v1/generate headers={
    "x-client-region": "%EF%BB%BF-us-west",
    "x-api-key": "redacted"
  } decision=route:europe-west-1 reason=client_region_parse_failed
```
Priya (SRE): oof — that %EF%BB%BF is the UTF-8 BOM bytes. does the SDK or their config file have a BOM? can you get a repro snippet from the customer?
Julia (Support): pasted their code (customer say they set region in a config file that they edit by hand):
```
// app config loader
const region = fs.readFileSync('/etc/app/region.txt', 'utf8');
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'x-client-region': region, 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' })
});
```
Julia (Support): they swore they wrote "us-west". i asked them to cat -v region.txt and they sent back: "^?us-west" (they didn't recognize it).
Matt (Eng): that ^? is likely BOM or other invisible Unicode char. our router parsing trims ascii whitespace but not unicode BOM or NBSP. when header=="﻿us-west" the region matcher fails and we fall back to default routing (EU for that tenant) — explains latency.
Priya (SRE): can repro locally — i did:
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H $'x-client-region: \xEF\xBB\xBFus-west' https://router-redwood.test/v1/generate
# router picked europe-west-1 (fallback)
```
Priya (SRE): attaching router debug: decision shows header present but parse_normalized='' after normalize step.
Julia (Support): customer workaround suggested — strip BOM from file or set region via env var. asked if we can do a quick server-side normalization to avoid other customers hitting this.
Matt (Eng): short-term fix: update edge header normalization to unicode-trim and remove BOM (\uFEFF) and other zero-width chars before region matching. prep PR to edge parsing lib. long-term: add logging metric when region parse fails that includes hex of first 8 bytes (sanitized) so we can triage similar invisible chars.
Priya (SRE): can we also allow explicit query param ?region=us-west as higher priority than header to help immediate customer?
Matt (Eng): yes, router supports query param precedence. will flip precedence for a 1hr hotfix for affected tenant only.
Julia (Support): updated customer with both workaround (remove BOM) + we will deploy hotfix to respect ?region for their tenant. customer will roll their config fix too.
RouterBot: rollout scheduled: edge-normalize-bom fix -> canary 20% @ 2026-03-15T11:00Z, tenant-scoped region-param-precedence -> immediate patch @ 2026-03-15T09:40Z.
Priya (SRE): created internal ticket RED-2456, assigned to Matt. follow-up: add unit tests for header values with BOM, NBSP, zero-width no-break space.
Julia (Support): closing loop with customer in support ticket, marking as "escalated -> resolved (hotfix + customer config)". :white_check_mark:
Matt (Eng): PR opened: edge/parse: strip_unicode_whitespace_and_bom(). will link MR to RED-2456.
Priya (SRE): nice catch. lesson: invisible chars in hand-edited config files are a real pain. :facepalm:
